knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector

question.:question/problem: Let $b=\begin{bmatrix}20 \\ -21\end{bmatrix}$. Find a unit vector that is parallel to $b$ and points the same direction.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
u=\frac{b}{|b|}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
|b| &= \sqrt{(20)^2+(-21)^2} \\
&= \sqrt{400+441} \\
&= \sqrt{841} \\
&= 29
\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}
u &= \frac{b}{|b|} \\
&= \frac{1}{29}\cdot (b) \\
&= \frac{1}{29}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}20 \\ -21\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}\frac{20}{29} \\ - \frac{21}{29}\end{bmatrix}
\end{aligned}
$$
